verdict.rationale: Gitleaks documents its own pre-commit hook, which fails a commit that contains a secret. It also documents dir and stdin scan modes, so code is checked before it lands no matter who wrote it, including an agent. There is no coding-agent-specific integration, such as agent hooks, an MCP server or llms.txt (the llms.txt probe returned 404), and scanning covers only secrets, not broader issues. missing for 10: documented coding-agent integration (agent hooks/MCP/tool definition), agent-oriented docs or llms.txt, scanning beyond hardcoded secrets, hands-on corroboration of agent workflows.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can wire the scanner into my coding agent so AI-generated code is scanned for issues before it lands

citations.quote: You can run Gitleaks as a pre-commit hook by copying the example `pre-commit.py` script into your `.git/hooks/` directory.
You can also stream data to gitleaks with the `stdin` command. Example: `cat some_file | gitleaks -v stdin`
